question.problem:
Find the Laplace transform $Y(s)=L\{y(t)\}$ if 

$$
{y}^{′}+4y={u}_{\pi /2}(t)\cdot sin\,(3t-\frac{3\pi }{2})\,,\,y(0)=-2,
$$

where ${u}_{\pi /2}(t)=u\,(t-\frac{\pi }{2})$ is the unit step function.

You may make use of the following result:

$$
L\{\operatorname{sin}⁡\omega t\}=\frac{\omega }{{s}^{2}+{\omega }^{2}},\,s>0
$$

$Y(s)=-\frac{2}{s+4}\,+\,$
{{field-1}},$\,s>0$
question.worked_solution:
First, we take the Laplace transform of both sides and use the addition and scalar multiplication properties of the Laplace transform:

$$
\begin{aligned}L\{{y}^{′}+4y\} & =L\{{u}_{\pi /2}(t)\cdot sin\,(3t-\frac{3\pi }{2})\} \\ L\{{y}^{′}\}+4L\{y\} & =L\{{u}_{\pi /2}(t)\cdot sin\,(3t-\frac{3\pi }{2})\}\end{aligned}
$$

To calculate $L\{{y}^{′}\},$ we use the formula for the Laplace transform of a derivative and the initial condition $y(0)=-2:$

$$
L\{{y}^{′}\}=sY(s)-y(0)=sY(s)-(-2)=sY(s)+2
$$

To find the transform of the right-hand side, we note that the term 

$$
{u}_{\pi /2}(t)\cdot sin\,(3t-\frac{3\pi }{2})
$$

is in the form $u(t-a)\cdot f(t)$ where $a=\frac{\pi }{2}$ and $f(t)=sin\,(3t-\frac{3\pi }{2}).$ This can be interpreted as time-delayed sinusoidal forcing. 

Now, recall that the second shifting theorem (time-shifting property) states

$$
L\{u(t-a)\cdot f(t)\}={e}^{-as}\cdot L\{f(t+a)\}.
$$

  

So, by the second shifting theorem, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}L\{u\,(t-\frac{\pi }{2})\cdot sin\,(3t-\frac{3\pi }{2})\} & ={e}^{-(\pi /2)s}\cdot L\{sin\,(3\,(t+\frac{\pi }{2})-\frac{3\pi }{2})\} \\  & ={e}^{-(\pi /2)s}\cdot L\{\operatorname{sin}⁡(3t)\} \\  & ={e}^{-(\pi /2)s}\cdot \frac{3}{{s}^{2}+9} \\  & =\frac{3{e}^{-\pi s/2}}{{s}^{2}+9}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we substitute these back into our transformed differential equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}L\{{y}^{′}\}+4L\{y\} & =L\{{u}_{\pi /2}(t)sin\,(3t-\frac{3\pi }{2})\} \\ (sY(s)+2)+4Y(s) & =\frac{3{e}^{-\pi s/2}}{{s}^{2}+9} \\ (s+4)Y(s)+2 & =\frac{3{e}^{-\pi s/2}}{{s}^{2}+9} \\ (s+4)Y(s) & =-2+\frac{3{e}^{-\pi s/2}}{{s}^{2}+9} \\ Y(s) & =-\frac{2}{s+4}+\frac{3{e}^{-\pi s/2}}{({s}^{2}+9)(s+4)}\end{aligned}
$$
